title: Ollie, a privacy-focused AI assistant, is shutting down
text: As an increasing number of AI assistants flood the market, the founder of Ollie, an assistant that respected its users' privacy, says it will be shutting down in a week.

title: Intel’s stock crashes, knocking $12B from government’s stake
text: Intel is being hurt by PC sales as the AI industry gobbles memory and other components causing PC prices to rise.

title: Anthropic expected to receive high ‘junk’ rating from credit agencies following IPO, FT report says
text: Blackstone's forecast is just a prediction, but naturally, a high junk rating would make it more difficult and costlier for Anthropic to raise the money to keep funding its massive spending that has undergirded its business.

title: Last-minute Halloween costumes for tech nerds
text: No Halloween costume? Just be a deceptively cute AI agent icon, a PHP vulnerability, or sleepy time Bryan Johnson.

title: Cracks are emerging in the AI spending boom
text: Big Tech is pouring billions into AI infrastructure, but mounting debt, negative cash flow, and growing investor skepticism are raising questions about the sustainability of the AI spending boom.

title: Zest’s new AI agent finds restaurants and books reservations over text
text: Can't agree on where to eat? Zest's AI concierge can combine everyone's tastes, put restaurant options to a vote, and make the reservation.

title: Google’s first data center satellite is online and writing poetry
text: The first TPU in space is running a Google DeepMind Gemma 4 model and writing cheesy poetry.

title: Theranos whistleblower Tyler Shultz warns that the AI boom is ‘a great opportunity to go deceive people’
text: The cautionary Theranos tale takes on a new significance in the AI era, when companies that have never turned a profit are raising capital at trillion-dollar valuations.

title: DoorDash said it’s only received ‘several hundred’ orders from AI agents
text: DoorDash said that it is open to working with third-party agent makers.

text: 5 days to save up to $100, plus a second pass for free to TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 in Boston on November 4. Register now.

title: Can AI data centers be mass-produced like cars? This startup aims to find out
text: Runware is building a factory to turn out prefabricated AI data centers on an assembly line. The real test will be whether it can deliver at that scale.

title: Making it easier for websites to express AI training preferences
text: OpenAI will honor a shared robots.txt signal to help website operators communicate their AI training preferences to participating providers.

title: Community safety report and new protections for teens
text: OpenAI is strengthening violence prevention in ChatGPT with expanded safeguards, earlier interventions, and a new commitment to public safety reporting.

title: You don’t need to believe in a god to get a religious exemption from using AI at work
text: David Durman, a University of Kentucky administrator, recently earned a religious exemption from using AI in the workplace.

title: Fair use benefits everyone
text: OpenAI shares excerpts from court briefs by creators, academics, accessibility advocates, and legal experts, among others, on how fair use supports AI training and innovation.

title: AWS will be a $1T business, Jassy says — but first, it will spend big
text: Amazon wants to be the king of AI cloud computing and become the first $1 trillion revenue business. But to do that it will have to continue on its capex spending spree, its CEO said Thursday.

title: As search traffic dries up, Reddit announces it’s shifting to a logged-in experience
text: As AI transforms how people find information online, Reddit is rethinking its open-web roots to protect its audience and business.
